instructions: The night before, or at least 1 hour ahead: melt 4 tbsp of the butter and stir it in a bowl with 2 tsp of the milk, 1 egg yolk, the vanilla and 2/3 cup (140 g) of the sugar. Stir in 1 1/4 cups (150 g) of the all-purpose flour, the baking powder, the baking soda and a pinch of the salt, until it's crumbly. Press it into a log about 2 inches thick, wrap it, and refrigerate.
Warm 3/4 cup (180 g) of the milk to 100 to 110°F, which feels barely warm on your wrist. Stir in 1/3 cup (70 g) of the sugar and the yeast. Leave it about 5 minutes, until it's foamy.

In a large bowl or a stand mixer, add the yeast mixture, the cream, 1 whole egg, the bread flour, 1 3/4 cups (225 g) all-purpose flour and 1 tsp salt. Mix on low for about 2 minutes, until a dough forms.
Add 3 1/2 tbsp of softened butter and knead on medium for about 14 minutes. The dough is ready when it's smooth and stretches into a thin, nearly see-through sheet.
Shape it into a ball, cover it, and let it rise in a warm spot for about 1 hour, until doubled.

Punch the dough down and divide it into 16 pieces, about 62 g each. Roll each into a smooth ball and set them about 2 inches apart on two lined baking sheets. Cover loosely and let them rise 30 to 45 minutes, until doubled.
Meanwhile, whisk the 2 remaining egg yolks with 2 tsp milk and 1/2 tsp sugar, and refrigerate it. Heat the oven to 350°F near the end of the rise.
Slice the chilled log into 16 pieces. Flatten each between two sheets of plastic wrap into a disk about 2 1/2 inches wide, and lay one on each ball of dough.
Brush the disks with the egg wash, let it dry for a minute, and brush again.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes, until the tops are golden and the bottoms are lightly browned. Let them sit in the pan 5 minutes, then move them to a rack.

Serve warm or at room temperature. Keep the cooled bolo bao in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Don't put them in the fridge. For longer, freeze them in a zip-top bag for up to 1 month and reheat from frozen at 350°F for about 10 minutes.
advance_prep_notes: make the topping dough the night before and chill it
method_notes: The lead is Omnivore's Cookbook (4.94 from 30): an enriched dough with milk, cream and one egg, and a butter-sugar topping disk with a crackly top. It makes 16 buns, so the batch keeps 4 days of snacks; leftovers freeze well. King Arthur (4.8 from 16) uses a tangzhong dough and an optional custard filling; both agree on a 350°F oven and baking until golden. Despite the name, there is no pineapple in it. The lead's amounts are written in cups and grams.
